note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Adult male with ~3 days of acute gastroenteritis symptoms: profuse watery diarrhoea, crampy central abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting (worse with dairy), feverish sensation; no blood in stool. Ongoing fluid losses with hydration concerns. Plan emphasizes oral rehydration and supportive care with follow-up in 48 hours if symptoms persist.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute gastroenteritis with watery diarrhoea and GI symptoms
  - Timeline: Onset ~3 days ago; diarrhoea occurs about hourly when awake; crampy abdominal pain; associated nausea and vomiting (particularly after milk); no bloody stool reported.
  - Associated symptoms: feverish feeling; dehydration risk suggested by volume loss; reduced appetite/solid intake; appetite variable; last solid intake today with loose stools.
  - Systems review: GI symptoms predominant; no diarrheal blood; urinary symptoms not prominent; no documented weight loss or fever measurement; no nocturnal symptoms recorded.
  - Social history/Medications/Exam findings: Lives with sister and mother; works in government in Central London; smokes socially; drinks alcohol infrequently; no regular medications; no listed allergies; examination findings not documented; no vitals provided.
  - Differential: Gastroenteritis (acute infectious gastroenteritis suspected). No red flags documented (e.g., GI bleeding, severe dehydration requiring immediate ED).

Issue 2:
- Impact on daily living and activity
  - Timeline/Symptoms: Drinking fluids and attempting to stay hydrated; continuing work attendance despite symptoms; overall functional impact acknowledged.
  - Systems review: Functional impairment related to GI illness; no additional systemic complaints beyond GI.
  - Social history/Medications/Exam findings: See Issue 1 for social history; no new meds beyond intermittent paracetamol; exam findings not documented.
  - Plan considerations: Supportive care to enable functioning; no additional diagnostics indicated at this time.

Issue 3:
- Family history of colon cancer
  - Timeline/Symptoms: Father has colon cancer, currently in advanced stage; details uncertain.
  - Systems review/Medications/Exam: Not directly actionable in current visit; no direct patient symptoms attributed to this history.
  - Social history/Medications/Exam findings: Family history noted; no related patient symptoms recorded.
  - Plan considerations: Acknowledged as relevant family history; no preventive actions specified in this visit.

Medications:
- Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented
- Diarolyte (oral rehydration solution) — dose/route/frequency not documented

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies reported

Past Medical History:
- None reported; patient states otherwise fit and well; no regular medications

Social History:
- Lives with mother and sister
- Works in an office in Central London (government)
- Smokes socially
- Alcohol: occasional beer; may drink more on weekends/friends occasions
- No regular medications

Preventative History:
- Not documented

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented
- Exam findings: Not documented

Plan:
- Hydration and diet
  - Start oral rehydration with Diarolyte; remaining fluids should be clear fluids
  - Soft diet (e.g., soup, mash); gradually reintroduce solids as tolerated
- Medications
  - Paracetamol as needed for fever/pain; dose/route/frequency not documented
  - Avoid or limit alcohol intake
- Safety net and follow-up
  - If symptoms not settling within 48 hours, contact/return for reassessment
  - If dehydration signs develop, further investigations may be considered
  - Continue monitoring tolerance to fluids and overall clinical status
- Patient education
  - Focus on maintaining hydration; use Diarolyte as advised and drink fluids regularly
  - Clear fluids preferred initially; avoid dairy if milk-triggered vomiting is suspected
  - Reassurance that symptoms are consistent with gastroenteritis and expected to improve over next few days
- Additional notes
  - Doctor mentioned that dehydration would prompt further testing/investigation if needed
